THE ESSENTIALS

What is an Activity Amendment?

In the UAE, your company is only legally permitted to conduct the exact business activities listed on your official Trade License. Operating outside this scope is a serious violation.

If your business expands into new markets—for example, a software consultancy deciding to start e-commerce trading—you must officially amend your license. This process updates the government registry, modifies your corporate documents (MOA), and ensures your banking compliance remains intact.

When to Amend

  • Scaling Operations: Launching new services not covered by your initial setup.
  • Business Pivots: Changing direction entirely (e.g., from marketing to real estate).
  • Removing Constraints: Dropping unused activities to reduce renewal costs.
THE RISK

Operating Outside Licensed Activities

Invoicing for services or products not listed on your trade license creates significant legal and financial exposure.

Compliance Fines

Government inspectors routinely audit corporate invoices. Billing for activities not explicitly stated on your license can trigger instant fines ranging from AED 5,000 to AED 50,000.

Bank Account Freezes

When incoming funds do not match your approved business profile (e.g., a software company receiving payments for real estate brokering), banks flag the account for suspected money laundering and will freeze funds.

Contract Invalidation

If you enter into a contract to provide a service you are not licensed for, UAE courts may declare the contract null and void, leaving you with no legal recourse to collect payments.

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Companies often pivot, expand their services, or adapt to new market demands. Changing or adding a business activity legally allows your company to trade in new products or offer new services that were not covered under your original Trade License.

Yes. Most Freezone and Mainland jurisdictions allow you to bundle multiple related activities (e.g., IT consulting and software development) under one license. Unrelated activities may require separate licenses or additional approvals.

The limit depends on the licensing authority. Many Freezones allow up to 3 to 5 activities under the same license category without extra charges. Adding more activities or mixing commercial and professional activities often incurs additional fees.

Yes, regulated activities such as healthcare, education, food trading, or financial services often require No Objection Certificates (NOCs) from relevant government bodies (e.g., DHA, KHDA, Dubai Municipality) before the activity can be added.

Yes, you can apply for an activity amendment at any point during your license validity. However, if your license is close to expiring, it is highly recommended to process the activity change simultaneously with your license renewal to save on amendment fees.

It can. If your new activity changes your business model significantly or moves you into a high-risk sector, your bank may request an updated profile or compliance review. You must always submit the amended Trade License to your bank immediately.

Not necessarily, unless your current company name implies a specific activity that you are removing (e.g., dropping 'Consulting' for 'Trading'). In such cases, an authority might request a name change alongside the activity change.

Standard activity amendments without external approvals usually take 3 to 5 business days. If external government approvals (NOCs) are required, the timeline will depend on the specific regulatory body's processing time.

Standard requirements include a copy of your current Trade License, a Board Resolution requesting the change, and passport copies of the shareholders. We will prepare the Board Resolution for you.

Generally, no. Your existing visas remain valid as long as the company itself remains active and compliant. The activity change primarily affects the Trade License and Memorandum of Association.

Yes. When you change or add business activities, your company's MOA must be amended to reflect the new operational scope. This is a mandatory legal step that we handle as part of the service.
